claims.claim: Complement equivalence and exact endpoint cases. Let F(n,k) count labelled graphs on [n] with vertex-cover number at most k, let N=binom(n,2), and put m=n−k. For 0≤k≤n, F(n,k)=2^N−T(n,m), where T(n,m) is the number of labelled K_m-free graphs. Consequently F(n,n−3)=2^N−T(n,3), with T(n,3) the triangle-free graph count. Also F(n,0)=1; F(n,1)=1+n(2^{n−1}−1)−binom(n,2); F(n,n−2)=2^N−1; and F(n,n−1)=F(n,n)=2^N.
claims.evidence: For every graph, τ(G)=n−α(G). Thus τ(G)≤k iff G has an independent m-set, and complementation bijects the graphs without such a set with K_m-free graphs. For m=0, the empty clique is present in every graph, so T(n,0)=0. The endpoint formulas then follow directly; the k=1 formula correctly applies inclusion-exclusion to the n labelled stars.
claims.witness: For k=1, the empty graph contributes once, each one-edge graph is counted twice among its two possible star centers and needs one subtraction, and every admissible graph with at least two edges has a unique common center.
claims.search_method: Direct bijection and endpoint case analysis, followed by exhaustive exact enumeration for n≤6.

claims.claim: Two-sided family-size lower bounds. For 2≤m≤n, put r=m−1, write n=ar+s with 0≤s<r, and let e(n,m)=[n²−s(a+1)²−(r−s)a²]/2. Then T(n,m)≥2^{e(n,m)} and F(n,n−m)≥2^{N−binom(m,2)}. For fixed m≥3, e(n,m)=(m−2)n²/[2(m−1)]+O_m(1); specifically e(n,3)=floor(n²/4).
claims.evidence: All subgraphs of a fixed balanced complete (m−1)-partite graph are K_m-free, yielding exactly 2^{e(n,m)} distinct examples. Fixing an m-set to be independent leaves N−binom(m,2) freely selectable edges and gives the F lower bound. Algebraically, e=(m−2)n²/[2(m−1)]−s(m−1−s)/[2(m−1)], proving the stated fixed-m error and the m=3 specialization.
claims.witness: The balanced-partition construction and fixed-independent-set construction inject Boolean edge choices into T and F respectively.
claims.search_method: Constructive counting proof and exact finite verification for every 2≤m≤n≤6.

claims.claim: Enumeration-strategy obstruction and its sharp endpoint boundary. For every fixed m≥3, both F(n,n−m) and T(n,m) have 2^{Θ(n²)} members. More generally, if m≥3 and k=n−m≥cn for a constant c>0, both families have 2^{Ω(n²)} members. Thus an algorithm that explicitly lists every admissible graph, or instead every K_m-free graph before subtracting from 2^N, cannot run in 2^{o(n²)} time in this regime. At m=2, T(n,2)=1, whereas at m=3 already T(n,3)≥2^{floor(n²/4)}; hence k=n−3 is the first fixed-distance-from-n endpoint where neither side can be explicitly enumerated within the target time. This does not prove a lower bound against implicit exact counting.
claims.evidence: For fixed m, the preceding F lower bound has exponent N−O_m(1), while the bipartite construction gives T≥2^{floor(n²/4)}; 2^N is a common upper bound. More generally q=k(2n−k−1)/2≥k(n−1)/2=Ω(n²) when k≥cn. Explicit listing therefore takes at least one operation per family member. K_2-free means edgeless, while the bipartite construction already gives the asserted m=3 jump. The claim correctly limits the obstruction to explicit enumeration.
claims.witness: T(n,2)=1, whereas a fixed balanced bipartition supplies 2^{floor(n²/4)} distinct triangle-free graphs.
claims.search_method: Asymptotic analysis of the constructive lower bounds and the trivial 2^N upper bound; finite constituent bounds were checked exactly.

claims.claim: There is a deterministic exact algorithm using polynomial space and time 2^{q+O(n)}, where q=binom(n,2)−binom(n−k,2)=kn−k(k+1)/2. Therefore the target is achieved whenever k=o(n), including k=O(n/log n).
claims.evidence: For each k-set C there are exactly 2^q graphs with no edge outside C. Retaining a generated graph only for its lexicographically first k-cover counts every graph with τ≤k exactly once, because every smaller cover extends to a k-cover. At most binom(n,k)^2·2^q polynomial-time tests are used, which is 2^{q+O(n)}, and enumeration needs only the current graph, subset iterators, and polynomial-bit counters. Since q≤nk, k=o(n) makes the exponent o(n²).
claims.witness: The unique retained pair is (G,C), where C is the first k-element vertex cover of G.
claims.search_method: Direct correctness, runtime, space, and asymptotic analysis of the stated enumeration algorithm.

claims.claim: Structural hard-strip reduction. For n≥2 let ℓ(n)=floor(n/ceil(log₂n)). A deterministic exact 2^{o(n²)}-time algorithm for every 0≤k≤n exists if and only if one exists uniformly on the restricted strip ℓ(n)<k≤n−3. Equivalently, under m=n−k, the only unresolved range needed for the full target is 3≤m≤n−ℓ(n)−1.
claims.evidence: Restriction proves the forward implication. Conversely, k≤ℓ(n) is handled by claim 3 in exponent at most n²/ceil(log₂n)+O(n)=o(n²), k≥n−2 is handled by the endpoint formulas, and every remaining integer k lies in the stated strip. Translating k>ℓ(n) and k≤n−3 through m=n−k gives exactly 3≤m≤n−ℓ(n)−1.
claims.witness: The three branches k≤ℓ(n), ℓ(n)<k≤n−3, and k≥n−2 exhaust all valid k.

claims.claim: For every fixed k there is a polynomial-time exact algorithm. More explicitly, F(n,k) is computable in time at most poly(n)·sum_{t=0}^k binom(n,t)·2^{binom(t,2)+t}·[2(t+2)]^{2^t−1}.
claims.evidence: For a fixed cover C with I outside it independent, replacing a nonempty X⊆C by vertices of I yields a cover precisely when X is independent in G[C] and all of U_X are inserted. Hence C is minimum iff |U_X|≥|X| for every such X. Equality gives an alternative minimum cover, and standard subset lexicographic order makes C first exactly when U_X has no label below min X. The described capped-count/flag DP enforces precisely these conditions. Its state, transition, cover, and internal-edge bounds yield the displayed fixed-parameter factor, and summing exact cover sizes t≤k counts every qualifying graph once.
claims.witness: Exhaustive testing through n=5 found that the DP acceptance condition selects exactly the lexicographically first minimum cover of every labelled graph.
claims.search_method: Derived the cover-replacement characterization from scratch and exhaustively checked all graphs through n=5.

claims.claim: Exact first- and second-moment formulas give certified bounds for all parameters. For 1≤m≤n, let q=N−binom(m,2), S1=binom(n,m)2^q, and S2=binom(n,m)·sum_{j=max(0,2m−n)}^m binom(m,j)binom(n−m,m−j)2^{N−2binom(m,2)+binom(j,2)}. Then max{2^q, ceil(S1²/S2)}≤F(n,n−m)≤min{2^N,S1}. In particular, q≤log₂F(n,n−m)≤q+n.
claims.evidence: Let X count independent m-sets in a graph. Double counting (G,S) gives ΣX=S1. For ordered S,T with intersection j, exactly 2binom(m,2)−binom(j,2) distinct edges are forced absent, giving the stated S2=ΣX². The support inequalities 1_{X>0}≤X and (ΣX)²≤|supp X|ΣX² give the upper and second-moment lower bounds; fixing one independent set gives 2^q. Finally binom(n,m)≤2^n gives the logarithmic upper bound.
claims.witness: All S1 and S2 identities and both support bounds agree with exhaustive integer sums over every graph for n≤6.
claims.search_method: First- and second-moment double counting, Cauchy–Schwarz, and exhaustive exact verification.

claims.claim: At the triangle-free endpoint, a substantial subclass is exactly countable in polynomial time. Let B_n be the number of labelled bipartite graphs and P_n=sum_{a=0}^n binom(n,a)2^{a(n−a)}. Then B_0=1 and B_n=(P_n−sum_{a=1}^{n−1}binom(n,a)B_aB_{n−a})/2. Hence F(n,n−3)≤2^N−B_n is an exact-arithmetic, polynomial-time computable bound.
claims.evidence: P_n counts a graph together with an ordered proper two-coloring. A bipartite graph with c connected components has 2^c such colorings, which is also the number of ways to assign its components to two ordered labelled blocks. Therefore P_n=Σ_a binom(n,a)B_aB_{n−a}; isolating the a=0,n terms proves the recurrence. Its integer sizes and O(n²) convolution operations are polynomially bounded. Since every bipartite graph is triangle-free, B_n≤T(n,3), giving the stated upper bound on F.
claims.witness: Direct enumeration of bipartite graphs through n=6 exactly matches the recurrence and the triangle-free containment bound.
claims.search_method: Component-coloring double count, bit-complexity check, and exhaustive enumeration.

claims.claim: Direct distinguished-vertex recurrence for the triangle-free endpoint. Let 𝒯_r be the set of labelled triangle-free graphs on [r], and let i(H) include the empty set in the number of independent vertex sets of H. Then T(0,3)=1 and, for n≥1, T(n,3)=sum_{d=0}^{n−1} binom(n−1,d)·sum_{H∈𝒯_{n−1−d}} i(H)^d. Equivalently, T(n,3)=nT(n−1,3)+sum_{d=2}^{n−1} binom(n−1,d)·sum_{H∈𝒯_{n−1−d}} i(H)^d.
claims.evidence: Fixing a vertex v and its d-neighbor set S forces S to be independent. On the remaining vertices choose any triangle-free H; each labelled vertex of S may independently choose any independent set of H as its neighborhood. These choices are reversible and exclude every possible location of a triangle, proving the first recurrence. The d=0 term is T(n−1,3), while Σ_{H∈𝒯_{n−2}}i(H)=T(n−1,3) by the same one-distinguished-vertex construction, so the d=1 term is (n−1)T(n−1,3).
claims.witness: Both recurrence forms reproduce the exhaustive triangle-free counts for every 0≤n≤6.
claims.search_method: Reversible distinguished-vertex decomposition and exhaustive exact verification.

claims.claim: The distinguished-vertex recurrence gives a deterministic exact algorithm for F(n,n−3) in time poly(n)·2^{binom(n−3,2)} with exponential space, or time poly(n)·2^{binom(n−2,2)} with polynomial space, for n≥3. Both exponents remain Θ(n²), so neither algorithm achieves the requested 2^{o(n²)} strength.
claims.evidence: After consolidating d=0,1, every new moment uses r≤n−3. A subset-zeta transform over the binom(r,2) possible edges computes all i(H) values in polynomial times 2^{binom(r,2)} time and comparable exponential space. Alternatively, enumerating all graphs H and all 2^r vertex subsets computes i(H) in polynomial space and time 2^{binom(r,2)+r}=2^{binom(r+1,2)}, maximized at r=n−3 as claimed. Polynomially many smaller orders and moments do not change either exponent. Both binomial exponents are asymptotic to n²/2.
claims.witness: The checker verifies the identity i(H)=g(complement(E(H))) for the stated subset-zeta construction on every graph through r=5, as well as the recurrence it evaluates.
claims.search_method: Operation count, memory analysis, exponent maximization, and exact validation of the zeta identity.

target_evidence: The source asks for one exact 2^{o(n²)}-time algorithm covering all input pairs (n,k). The draft proves such performance for k=o(n), fixed k, and the elementary high-k endpoints, and it isolates the remaining strip. It does not construct the assumed strip algorithm; in particular, its exact k=n−3 algorithms have exponent asymptotic to n²/2. Thus it supplies correct material progress without proving the entire target. Its claimed resolution is PARTIAL, which accurately describes this coverage.
